items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: So I tried to get Lorenzo Teo to teach me. I went to Lorenzo's house. He was staying on Seminar Street. I went to Lorenzo's house. And he agreed to teach me.

ctx.x: Did anybody have a banging system at all in those days that you knew?

Not that I know of, you know. Mm-hmm. And, um, well I took it and tried to practice on it. I didn't know what I was doing. So I tried to get Lorenzo Teo to teach me. I went to Lorenzo's house. He was staying on Seminar Street. I went to Lorenzo's house. And he agreed to teach me. He told me, he said, he told me to go buy a book. I told Angie and come to his house the following Wednesday.
Is that the young Lorenzo Teo? Yes.

items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: Renzi Teo was supposed to teach me. I went to see him, he was supposed to teach me.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. Mm-hm. No, I don't. Were you playing regular with Wooden D uppterville? Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

Yeah, we had no ride. How'd you do it? Just the same as we did with the others at John's Unyall. Just walking cold, huh? Yeah. Well, I guess you knew each other. Yeah. It seemed more of a band out of the same little team. You'd played together before. I wanted to get back to your addresses. You lived in the 2100 block of Allen Street? The 2,100. 2,100? Mm-hmm. And you were just a young kid. I was just a kid. And how were you before you moved away from that? Oh, I must have been around about 9 or 10. And then…
